text:
Cole Hutson had the night of his young career on Friday: two goals, the second a wrister from the high slot with 6:54 left that gave Washington a 2-1 lead and an 86% chance to win. He finished it watching Sam Bennett celebrate the 200th goal of his career with 24 seconds to play, and the Panthers left Capital One Arena with a 3-2 win, their third straight.

Hutson opened the scoring on the power play at 10:26 of the first, from Ryan Leonard and Pierre-Luc Dubois, and the Capitals won that period 1.36 to 0.78 in expected goals (the quality of chances, added up). Jacob Markstrom kept it at one with the biggest save of the game, on Dubois from in close two minutes in. Florida took the second, 1.41 to 0.53, and Aaron Ekblad tied it on a power play at 4:51, with Brady Tkachuk and Matthew Tkachuk assisting. That pairing of brothers in Panthers sweaters is still new enough to look strange, and this week has been loud for both of them: several outlets, Sportsnet among them, asked whether Matthew should have been disciplined for his hit on Ottawa's Kleven, and NHL Player Safety did not act.

After Hutson's second, Florida came back with the kind of goals it has made a habit of. Eetu Luostarinen scored on a 4% snap shot at 15:42, set up by Brad Marchand and Anton Lundell, two nights after Marchand and Aleksander Barkov returned from injury. Then Matthew Tkachuk threw the puck toward the net from the right wall and Bennett tipped it in. NHL.com's Tom Gulitti reported the goal was reviewed for a hand pass by Ekblad and stood because Washington had played the puck first.

The game was close all night, and our replays of every shot gave Florida the win 55% of the time. Hutson led everyone with 0.49 wins added, Bennett was right behind at 0.48, and both goalies were near what their shots deserved. Florida also won 43 of 69 faceoffs. Gulitti reported Paul Maurice doesn't expect Garnet Hathaway, hurt in a third-period collision, to play against Tampa Bay on Saturday. For the Capitals, it is a loss that stings for how close it came, and a reminder that Hutson is quickly becoming one of the reasons to watch them.
headline: Bennett's 200th goal, with 24 seconds left, stuns Washington
